the encryption_version label against the payload it describes

prior_ledgers_read: f4de50ef6 -- the sender key helper this phase calls. Its findings were a doubled state fetch and a control that stopped applying; the second is why every control here was re-applied after each refactor.
da9ed20de -- the key cache. Its finding that a suite mocked the thing it claimed to prove is why the group send tests assert the request body rather than the absence of a throw.
0efe747b3 -- the display rule these messages are read back through.
51cde838c -- the extraction whose findings were surfaces painting ciphertext as text. The third finding below is that same defect arriving through a different door.
notes: Both pass 1 findings came from printing which branch each kind of conversation lands in, rather than reading the chain.

The probe that found them also printed a PLAINTEXT ON THE WIRE marker against the direct message rows, which was wrong: the probe mocks encryptMessage as RSA(content), so its ciphertext contains the secret by construction. The real function does not. A marker like that is only meaningful on rows whose content is not shaped by the mock.

The GROUP WITH other_user row that exposed the ordering defect is a shape the server cannot produce: user1_id is NULL for group rows, so GetOtherUserID returns 0 and the lookup finds nobody. The ordering was changed anyway, because the safety of an encryption decision rested on a column convention rather than on intent, and GetConversation populates other_user without the conversation_type guard its sibling list endpoint has.
The caller-supplied ciphertext label was likewise unreachable: every caller passes a version today. It becomes reachable the moment a group caller supplies one, which is G4.

Not fixed, and outside this frontend phase: the server still builds the pin event preview from encrypted_content and broadcasts it. The field is useless to every client now that the client ignores it. It is not a disclosure -- the ciphertext goes to a participant who already holds it -- but it is worth removing on the Go side.

usePinnedMessages contained both the right pattern and the wrong one. The pin mutation at line 118 spreads the real message from cache and only overrides pin metadata, guarded so it fabricates nothing when the message is absent. The websocket handler eighty lines below had diverged from it, and the diverged one was the path a server event reached.

Found both defects. Printed the request body for seven kinds of conversation: group, group carrying an other_user, direct message, direct message without one, mod mail, a caller supplying its own ciphertext, and media without text.

findings.summary: The recipient test was asked before the group test, so a group conversation carrying an other_user would have its message wrapped for that one member and every other member locked out, while it still looked properly encrypted. It cannot happen today only because user1_id is NULL for group rows -- a column convention holding up an encryption decision, in a handler that populates other_user without the conversation_type guard its sibling list endpoint has.

control.observed: AssertionError: expected 'v2' to be 'group-v1'. The group is RSA-wrapped for one member instead of sealed.

findings.summary: A caller that supplies its own ciphertext had it labelled plaintext. skipClientEncryption bypasses the encryption block, and encryption_version defaulted to plaintext whenever no version was given, so the label described the payload wrongly. Unreachable today because every caller passes a version, and reachable the moment a group caller supplies one.

control.observed: AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting. The unlabelled ciphertext is accepted and stored as plaintext.

findings.summary: The server builds a pin event's preview from the stored encrypted_content, cut to 120 characters. The client made a Message out of it with encryption_version 'unknown' -- a value no branch of the display rule tests -- so needsDecryption answered false and the pinned bar painted those characters as though they were the message. For a group message the cut also destroys the envelope, so nothing downstream could open it. Worse than a bad new row: merging replaces an entry by id, so a correct one fetched over REST was overwritten by the invented one.

control.observed: Two failures: expected 'v2:AAAAciphertext-cut-at-120-chars' to be 'v2:the-whole-real-ciphertext', and the refetch never happens -- expected getPinnedMessages to be called 2 times, but got 1.
